clue.text: Cry of approval in relative D

indicators.note: in places the cry of approval inside the word for a relative

parts.note: bro is short for brother, a relative
ole is the Spanish shout of approval heard at bullfights

explanation.surface: A shout of approval comes from a family member identified only by an initial.
explanation.walkthrough: Throughout this puzzle the bare letter D stands for the theme word, dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A bolero is a Spanish dance in triple time, one of the puzzle's many themed dances.

clue.text: Report of tree at the seaside

definitions.note: a phrase standing for a noun place, the shore by the sea

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the tree's name is taken by its sound

parts.note: the beech is a common broadleaf tree

explanation.surface: Someone hears news of a tree growing by the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A sandy shore is where one is when at the seaside, so the place stands for the phrase.

clue.text: Husband of famous horsewoman makes sign on day 100

parts.note: Leo is a sign of the zodiac
Fri is the abbreviation for Friday
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A rider's spouse produces a signal on the hundredth day.
explanation.walkthrough: The famous horsewoman is Lady Godiva, who by legend rode naked through Coventry; her husband was the Earl of Mercia.
explanation.definitionFit: The Anglo-Saxon earl was married to Lady Godiva, the legendary naked rider of Coventry.

clue.text: Went back to be given further therapy?

definitions.meaning: withdrew or retired, as an army does
the question mark flags the split

explanation.definitionFit: Retreat means withdraw, and split as re-treat it means treat medically once more.

clue.text: Cure for hysteria partly shown in film

indicators.note: shown in puts the fragment inside the word for a film

parts.note: pic is informal for a picture or film

indicators.note: partly means only a portion of the word hysteria is used, its opening run

explanation.surface: A remedy for hysteria is partly depicted in a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cure for hysteria' looks like the definition, but only 'Cure' defines; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Physic is an old word for medicine, a remedy or cure.

clue.text: Man and boy with femme fatale

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man
Len is a boy's name, short for Leonard

explanation.surface: A man and a boy keep company with a seductive woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The femme fatale is Helen of Troy, whose elopement started the Trojan War.
explanation.definitionFit: Helen of Troy is the archetypal fatal beauty whose abduction led to war.

clue.text: D before deal?

parts.note: a dance step with dragging feet, and also the mixing of cards a dealer does before dealing a hand

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a foot-dragging dance and the card mixing done before a deal.

clue.text: Repetitive D

parts.note: a Latin dance whose name is one syllable said three times over

explanation.definitionFit: The Latin American dance has a name made of the same syllable three times, hence repetitive.

clue.text: Put cross without point in entry for D

indicators.note: in places the shortened vote inside the gateway word

parts.note: a gate is an entrance or way of entry

indicators.note: without means the point letter is dropped

parts.note: to put a cross on a ballot paper is to vote
E is east, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone marks a cross, omitting a point, in an entry about a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' drops E from VOTE to leave VOT, which goes 'in' GATE.
explanation.definitionFit: The gavotte is an old French dance in moderate duple time.

clue.text: Relating to covering of lung, all pure fiction

indicators.note: fiction is something made up, so these letters are reinvented in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Claims about the membrane round the lung are all pure invention.
explanation.definitionFit: The pleura is the membrane lining the lungs, and the adjective describes things belonging to it.

clue.text: Waller goes up west in division of administration

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Fats Waller was a famous American jazz pianist and composer

indicators.note: in places the compass letter inside the branching word

parts.note: a fork is a point where a road or river divides

explanation.surface: A jazzman heads west within a branch of government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes up' turns FATS into STAF; then 'in' puts W into FORK to give FWORK.
explanation.definitionFit: Staff work is the planning and administrative work done by officers behind the front line.

clue.text: Ferryman going about in case of D

indicators.note: going about means the ferryman's name surrounds the other piece

parts.note: Charon ferried the dead across the Styx in Greek myth
lest means for fear that, in case

explanation.surface: A boatman goes round as a precaution for a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The Charleston is a lively 1920s dance named after the South Carolina city.

clue.text: Backing of hospital for north Alpine wind

indicators.note: backing means the little word that follows is turned around

parts.note: the clue word of supplies its own two letters
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A hospital's support for a northern wind in the Alps.
explanation.definitionFit: The foehn is a warm dry wind blowing down the lee side of the Alps.

clue.text: Nearly choose books on lace work

indicators.note: on in an across clue means the books follow the first piece
nearly means the verb loses its last letter

parts.note: to pick is to choose
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: Someone almost selects books about lacemaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A picot is a small decorative loop worked into the edge of lace.

clue.text: Outstanding excavation almost immediately put outside

indicators.note: put outside means the shortened word wraps around the dig
almost means the word for immediately loses its last letter

parts.note: pronto means at once, immediately
a mine is an excavation dug for minerals

explanation.surface: An outstanding dig is promptly moved outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims PRONTO to PRONT, which is 'put outside' MINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Prominent means standing out, conspicuous or outstanding.

clue.text: Fire sergeant for D

parts.note: a flame is fire
a sergeant is a non-commissioned officer, NCO

explanation.surface: A fiery sergeant is put forward for a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Flamenco is the passionate Andalusian dance of stamping feet.

clue.text: Place trap with result being upset

definitions.text: Place trap with result being upset

indicators.note: being upset means the words place and trap are tipped over and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sets a snare and everything is overturned.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue plays on the idiom 'upset the applecart', to spoil a plan.
explanation.definitionFit: To upset the applecart is to ruin plans, which is just what a trap does when sprung.

clue.text: How about marshal of French melon?

indicators.note: about means the word how surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: Michel Ney was one of Napoleon's marshals
de is French for of

explanation.surface: A question about a French marshal's fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Michel Ney was a famous marshal of Napoleon, executed in 1815.
explanation.definitionFit: Honeydew is a variety of melon with pale green sweet flesh.

clue.text: Off with his head? Get it done

definitions.meaning: an order for a beheading, putting someone to death
carry out or perform a task

explanation.definitionFit: Execute means both to put to death and to carry out a plan.

clue.text: Top people in Pennsylvania D

indicators.note: in places the topped word inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: PA is the postal abbreviation for Pennsylvania

indicators.note: top means the first letter of the word for people is removed

parts.note: folk means people

explanation.surface: Elite folk in Pennsylvania take to a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' removes F from FOLK to leave OLK; 'Top people' looks like the elite.
explanation.definitionFit: The polka is a lively Bohemian couple dance.

clue.text: Allow the unions the last of the salad

parts.note: let means allow
TUC is the Trades Union Congress, Britain's federation of trade unions

indicators.note: last of takes the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Unions are allowed the remainder of the salad.
explanation.walkthrough: The TUC is the national body of British trade unions.
explanation.definitionFit: Lettuce is the leafy plant used as the base of most salads, standing for the dish.

clue.text: Setter's followed end of hadj with D

indicators.note: followed means the setter's piece comes after the other one
end of picks the final letter of the pilgrimage word

parts.note: the setter speaks as I, and I've is short for I have

explanation.surface: The compiler has followed the close of a pilgrimage with a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Jive is a lively dance to swing or rock and roll music.

clue.text: Country for left winger in D

parts.note: Turkey is a country
Trot is short for Trotskyist, a left-wing radical

explanation.surface: A country swaps for a radical at a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The turkey trot was a ragtime dance popular in the early twentieth century.

clue.text: D adds zest to love

indicators.note: to means the zest piece is attached in front of the love piece

parts.note: tang means a sharp zesty flavour
O is love, a nil score in tennis

explanation.surface: A dance gives extra zest to romance.
explanation.definitionFit: The tango is the sultry Argentine couple dance.

clue.text: Tree — let me see — with product of old rope

parts.note: the oak is a tree
um is a hesitant sound, as when saying let me see

explanation.surface: Someone pondering a tree considers what old rope makes.
explanation.definitionFit: Oakum is loose fibre picked from old ropes, used for caulking ships.

clue.text: Live money without a D

parts.note: to be is to exist or live

indicators.note: without means the letter a is dropped

parts.note: a guinea is an old British gold coin worth 21 shillings

explanation.surface: Living on cash, minus a little, for a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' drops A from GUINEA, an old British coin, to leave GUINE.
explanation.definitionFit: The beguine is a Caribbean dance similar to a slow rumba.

clue.text: Extremes in fog for a D

indicators.note: in places the alphabet extremes inside the gloom word

parts.note: murk is gloom or fog
A and Z are the extremes of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Extremes of weather in the fog lead to a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The mazurka is a lively Polish folk dance in triple time.

clue.text: Torremolinos half shaken by this?

indicators.note: shaken means the half-name is jumbled up
half takes the first half of the resort name

explanation.surface: A Spanish resort is half shaken by a quake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes the first six letters, TORREM, which 'shaken' rearranges. Torremolinos is a Spanish holiday resort.
explanation.definitionFit: A tremor is a small earthquake, which could shake half a town.

clue.text: Current supplied by master switch

indicators.note: switch means the letters are swapped around into a new order

explanation.surface: Power is supplied through the main switch.
explanation.definitionFit: A stream is a current or steady flow, as of water or air.
